newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian securities prices rise on lower call money.
newsitem.headline: Indian securities prices rise on lower call money.

text.p: The securities prices rose on Thursday reacting to low call money rate of 0.25 percent, dealers said.
"Banks are parking their excess funds in securities mostly maturing in 1999-2002, pushing up their prices by almost 20-25 paise," Vinod Dixit, manager treasury at Centurion Bank, said.
The rally will continue until a fresh loan issue or the advance tax payments due on June 15 push up call rates, he said.

The 13.85 percent 2000 government stock rose to 104.95 rupees from its previous close 104.47 rupees, 11.64 percent 2000 to 99.35 rupees from 99.25 rupees, 12.14 percent 2000 to 100.50 rupees from 100.40 rupees, 12.69 percent 2002 to 100.93 rupees compared to its previous 100.90 rupees, a dealer said.
Yield on treasury bill maturing in April 1998 fell to 9.07 percent from previous 9.15 percent, he said.
